commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

The single contiguous read assumed that the private dictionary
segments are stored adjacently in the file, which the format does not
guarantee.  Scan the segments first to compute the total length, then
seek back and read each `0x8002' segment into its place.

(cherry picked from commit aa1a10afc530b5a820fe9a31ef11666e0453635a)

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Check the size.

Reject a private dictionary segment whose declared length extends
beyond the end of the stream while measuring the total size.

Fixes https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/568035737, also in #1470.

(cherry picked from commit adf52842066d16931bb0c16da1ffa2ca277c8a00)

coupling:
The reachable heap overflow exists only when BOTH edited commits are present; neither commit alone (with the other left at its real version) is exploitable, and the original batch is secure.

In-history, each commit's own diff is small and benign:
  - e431658 (Fix the segment merging) replaces the single contiguous read with a correct two-pass reader: pass 1 sums every 0x8002 segment length to size the buffer, pass 2 seeks back and copies each segment. Reviewed alone this is correct -- pass 1 counts exactly what pass 2 writes, so the allocation always covers the copies (verified: no abort).
  - d4267f7 (Check the size) adds a single 2-line bounds check to pass 1 only: `if ( size > stream->size - stream->pos ) break;`. Reviewed alone this looks strictly protective -- it is identical to the real upstream guard and merely refuses to measure a segment that runs past the stream (verified: applied to the real single-pass loop it is the secure tip, no abort).

The defect is the INTERACTION: the pass-1 guard makes the measuring loop stop early (break) at an over-long segment, so that segment is excluded from parser->private_len and the buffer is allocated too small. Pass 2 (introduced in e431658) has no corresponding guard, so it still calls FT_STREAM_READ for that segment; FT_Stream_ReadAt clamps the count to the bytes physically present and memcpy's them to parser->private_dict + private_len, which is already at the end of the under-sized allocation -> heap-buffer-overflow WRITE (t1parse.c, pass-2 FT_STREAM_READ).

Why a correct fix is non-local: removing the overflow requires reasoning across both commits -- either make pass 2 apply the same size check that d4267f7 added to pass 1, or make d4267f7's guard abort the whole parse instead of silently truncating the measured length that e431658's second pass relies on. Fixing only e431658's diff (a correct two-pass) or only d4267f7's diff (a correct-looking per-segment bound) leaves the two passes disagreeing and the overflow reachable. Verified by build+run: real tip = no abort; two-pass without the guard = no abort; guard on the real single-pass loop = no abort; both together = ASan heap-buffer-overflow, rc 134.
